headline: Acme Ledger is a capital-efficient leader in lender reconciliation; invest at USD 40-55M with milestones tied to enterprise churn
situation: Acme Ledger sells AI reconciliation software to 140 Indian NBFCs and SMB lenders, at ~USD 4.0M ARR growing ~2.1x YoY.
complication: Core-banking vendors are bundling basic reconciliation, and 38% of revenue sits with the top 5 customers.
resolution: Invest: a 9-month payback, 118% net revenue retention and RBI co-lending tailwinds outweigh concentration risk if diligence confirms churn.
key_takeaways: Product reduces reconciliation effort by ~70% at pilot lenders, giving a clear ROI story (₹2.4 Cr saved per lender per year).
Market is large and under-penetrated: USD 18B TAM, USD 4B SAM in India + SEA lenders.
Base case reaches USD 21M revenue by 2031 (51% CAGR); bull case USD 42M if SEA expansion lands.
Main risks are customer concentration and long enterprise sales cycles - both testable in diligence.
Entry at USD 40-55M implies 3.2-5.4x base-case MOIC over 5 years.
investment_thesis: Painful, budgeted problem | Lenders spend ~4% of opex on manual reconciliation
Proven ROI | ~70% effort reduction at pilot lenders
Data moat | 1,200+ lender-specific rules competitors lack
return_scenarios: Bear | USD 60M | 1.1x | Growth stalls at 28% CAGR, trade sale
Base | USD 210M | 3.8x | 51% CAGR, 10x revenue exit in 2031
Bull | USD 420M | 7.6x | SEA expansion lands, strategic acquirer premium
company_facts: Lead investors: Example Ventures, Sample Capital
market_headline: A USD 4B serviceable market is opening as RBI co-lending rules force lenders to automate reconciliation, and Acme is the only lender-native player
market_sizing: SAM: $4.0B (India + SEA NBFCs and SMB lenders)
competitors: CoreBank Suite | Large core-banking vendor; bundles basic recon | Acme is lender-workflow native, 3x faster go-live
ReconPro | Horizontal recon tool, USD 30M ARR | No lending-specific rules engine
In-house builds | Large banks build their own | Acme 60% cheaper over 3 years
moat_assessment: Proprietary data | High | 1,200+ lender rules and 30M reconciled loans
Switching costs | Medium | Embedded in month-end close; 6-week migration
Network effects | Low | Limited cross-lender benefit today
Regulatory know-how | Medium | RBI co-lending compliance built in
market_insights: Co-lending volumes grew 3x since 2024, multiplying reconciliation complexity.
Lenders spend ~4% of opex on manual operations - automation budget is real.
Acme's rules library (1,200+ lender rules) is a data moat competitors lack.
financial_headline: Base case reaches USD 21M revenue by 2031 with best-in-class unit economics, needing one more raise of ~USD 15M
financial_highlights: FY26 baseline ARR USD 4.0M (company-reported; partially verified).
Bear / base / bull CAGR of 28% / 51% / 70% over 2027-2031.
Gross margin ~78%, rising to 82% with automation.
Runway of 20 months; next raise ~USD 15M in 2027.
risk_headline: Overall risk is moderate (4.6/10); execution and concentration are the two risks diligence must clear
top_risks: Execution | Enterprise sales cycles of 6-9 months slow growth | Review pipeline conversion and sales hiring plan
Market | Core-banking vendors bundle free recon | Win-loss interviews with 10 lenders
Financial | Top-5 customers = 38% of revenue | Contract terms, renewal dates and churn history
Regulatory | RBI data-localisation changes | Legal review of data architecture
Exit | Limited Indian SaaS IPO path | Map strategic acquirers (core-banking, payments)
next_steps: Run 8-10 customer reference calls, prioritising top-5 accounts.
Obtain monthly ARR, cohort and churn data for the last 24 months.
Technical diligence on the rules engine and data security.
Model downside if the largest customer churns.
Negotiate milestone-based tranche tied to NRR above 110%.
